newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA METALS-Copper demand to outstrip supply.
newsitem.headline: INDIA METALS-Copper demand to outstrip supply.

text.p: India plans to raise its copper production at least five-fold by 2000, but a yawning supply and demand gap will remain due to surging domestic needs, industry officials and analysts said on Thursday.
"The gap will still be there in spite of a substantial anticipated rise in production," Tarun Jain, a senior official of private copper-maker Sterlite Industries (India) Ltd, told Reuters.
Company officials said the current annual demand for copper was about 300,000 tonnes compared with a domestic output of about 50,000 tonnes. India imports the rest of its requirement.
"Production will increase to about 250,000 tonnes by 2000 as new smelters start functioning but demand will also rise to about 400,000 tonnes," Jain said.
State-run Hindustan Copper Ltd is the monopoly copper producer in the country. Currently HCL operates smelters at Khetri in northwestern Rajasthan state and Ghatsila in eastern Bihar state.
HCL plans to raise the annual capacity of its Khetri smelter to 100,000 tonnes from the current 31,000 tonnes.
Sterlite is the only other firm to have a smelter with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes. It started operations in December 1996.
The Mines Ministry expects copper demand to increase to about 420,000 tonnes by 2000 and to 600,000 tonnes by 2005.
India threw open its closely-guarded metals and mining sector in 1993 to private sector investments.

Other private companies in the process of setting up smelters are Birla Copper, which is planning a copper smelter of 100,000 tonnes annual capacity, Metdist Industries Ltd, looking for a capacity of 150,000 tonnes and Swil Ltd with a capacity of 50,000 tonnes.

India has copper ore resources of about 732 million tonnes averaging 1.17 percent of copper. Out of this, eight working mines of HCL are estimated to contain 430 million tonnes of ore with an average grade of 1.21 percent copper representing 58.7 percent of the total ore resources in the country.
Analysts say India would continue to be a copper importer as mining of this low grade deposits is unprofitable.

Mines Ministry officials said although the mining cost per tonne of ore in India was comparable with other countries, the cost of the metal in concentrate worked out much higher because of the low grade of copper ore.

Company officials said that copper demand this season was dull on low offtake by the winding wire industry due to a mild summer but demand would pick up in the coming years as the power, electrical and electronics sectors develop.
"As power generation capacity goes up, copper demand will definitely rise for its use in power cables," a senior official at Birla Copper told Reuters.
The official said that the copper industry was trying to explore new areas to sell its produce such as use of copper tubes in buildings in place of galvanised pipes.
"The potential for copper in air-conditioning and refrigeration will also increase as disposable incomes rise," the official said.
Metal analysts said the demand for copper was growing at the rate of eight to 10 percent and the main potential for its expansion would be in the telecommunications industry.
"As the telecom sector develops the prospects of copper demand will widen," a Delhi-based analyst who did not wish to be identified said.
